title: dedicated-gpu-pool-scheduling-autoscale-warmup-debug-scratchpad
content:
Quick scratchpad / breadcrumbs for the dedicated GPU pool scheduling/autoscale incidents we've been seeing (capacity thrash + long warmup). Notes are noisy - mostly commands + outputs + hypotheses.

1) Incident summary
- Symptoms: recurring short spikes of queued inference pods (latency-sensitive routes) that trigger autoscaler to repeatedly add/remove nodes; observed scheduling failures (Pending: Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu) followed by long delays before pods actually start serving. Cold-start latency for new nodes often 3-6 minutes instead of target ~90s.
- Impact: client-facing tail latency spikes, higher unit cost due to churning nodes, occasional OOM/container runtime errors during device-plugin init.
- Relevant ticket: JIRA-INFRA-1245.

2) Timeline (notes)
- 2026-02-20 09:12: first alert from dashboards: queue length > 80 for route /chat-generation (p95 latency spike).
- 2026-02-20 09:13: autoscaler launched +4 nodes (scale request).
- 2026-02-20 09:16: nodes reported Ready ~3m. scheduler started binding pods but ~40 pods remained Pending for another 2-3m.
- 2026-02-20 09:20: CPU/GPU utilization low on new nodes but pods still initializing -> observed CrashLoop for device-plugin on 2 nodes.
- 2026-02-20 09:30: autoscaler observed low utilization and initiated scale-down, removing 3 nodes -> churn.

3) Commands tried + outputs (raw snippets)
- kubectl get pods -n infra | grep pending
  svc-gen-xxxxx   0/1 Pending   0     2026-02-20T09:13:20Z   

- kubectl describe pod svc-gen-xxxxx -n infra  <-- key lines
  Events:
    Type     Reason            Age                 From               Message
    ----     ------            ----                ----               -------
    Warning  FailedScheduling  2m (x15 over 5m)   default-scheduler  0/5 nodes are available: 5 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.

- kubectl get nodes -l pool=dedicated-gpu -o wide
  NAME                     STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION   INTERNAL-IP   EXTERNAL-IP
  gpu-node-xyz-1           Ready    <none>   4m    v1.26     10.0.0.12     34.120.1.2
  gpu-node-xyz-2           NotReady  <none>  2m    v1.26     10.0.0.13     34.120.1.3

- kubectl logs -n kube-system gpu-device-plugin-abc -c device-plugin
  E020 09:15:02.123 kubelet.go:xxx] device plugin registration timed out
  E020 09:15:05.456 plugin.go:yy] failed to open /dev/nvidia0: no such file or directory

- autoscaler logs (k8s-cluster-autoscaler)
  I0220 09:13:12 autoscaler.go: scale up: requesting 4 nodes (reason: pending pods 120)
  I0220 09:15:45 cloudprovider.go: provisioning: created 4 instances, request-id=proj-req-987
  I0220 09:16:48 autoscaler.go: scale up complete: 4 nodes, provision_time=3m36s
  I0220 09:22:00 autoscaler.go: scale down: removing 3 nodes (low utilization)

- prometheus query (approx)
  increase(kube_pod_container_status_phase{phase="Pending"}[10m]) -> spike from 5 -> 130 at 09:12
  node_boot_time_seconds -> observed average node ready_latency ~210s for gpu nodes

4) Observations / patterns
- Provision time is frequently > 3 minutes for GPU instances (image pulls + nvidia driver + device-plugin). We expected ~90s.
- Device-plugin driver issues: some nodes fail to register GPUs quickly (missing /dev/nvidia* until driver finishes). This leaves pods Pending even though node is Ready.
- Autoscaler configured with relatively aggressive target usage (target 0.65) and small cooldown (2m), which causes scale-down while pods still initializing -> thrash.
- Some pods are scheduled with podAntiAffinity/softSpread which can increase scheduling pressure and prevent packing new nodes efficiently.
- Image pull time matters: inference container images ~1.5GB; pulling on startup adds ~40-90s.

5) Hypotheses
- H1: Warmup window for new GPU nodes is insufficient; autoscaler sees low utilization quickly and scales down before device-plugin + runtime warmup completes, causing oscillation.
- H2: Driver/device-plugin installation is sometimes delayed (cloud-init ordering), so node reports Ready but GPUs not available for scheduling; kubelet Ready state is not a sufficient indicator for GPU readiness.
- H3: Target utilization/cooldown thresholds are too tight for bursty workloads; we need a larger buffer or warm pool.
- H4: Scheduling/pod distribution policies (anti-affinity, max-surge strategies) cause unnecessary fragmentation, increasing number of nodes required and triggering scale decisions.

6) Quick mitigations attempted (and results)
- Increased autoscaler cooldown to 6m (experiment on staging cluster) -> reduced churn but tail latency still present during biggest spikes.
- Toggled kubelet registrationGracePeriod / nodeReadyGrace to ensure GPU drivers finished before Ready? (hard to change quickly in prod) -> partial improvement in staging.
- Added pre-warm job during business hours: keep 2 nodes on as warm pool -> lowered p95 but cost increased.

7) Proposed longer-term fixes / runbook items
- Add a GPU readiness probe (custom node-exporter metric) that signals when device-plugin and /dev/nvidia* are present. Use that for autoscaler decisions (i.e., treat node as provisioned only after gpu_ready=true).
- Implement a warm pool / pre-warmed instance group for bursty routes (configurable by time-of-day).
- Increase autoscaler warmup / scale-down window to >= 8m for GPU pools; raise target utilization threshold slightly to reduce churn.
- Pre-pull large inference images via startup script or use local cache (image pre-pull DaemonSet while node initializing).
- Coordinate with infra to bake images with drivers + runtime (reduce driver install time). Consider using driver-enabled machine images.
- Revisit pod scheduling policies: relax anti-affinity and prefer packing on fewer nodes when pods are latency-sensitive.

8) Next actions (TODOs)
- [ ] Run staged experiment: autoscaler cooldown 8m + GPU-ready metric gating in staging (owner: Maya).
- [ ] Add a simple prometheus alert: gpu_node_ready_latency > 180s (owner: Luis).
- [ ] Prototype image pre-pull DaemonSet (owner: Kevin).
- [ ] Draft runbook for on-call: detection steps + immediate mitigations (keep warm pool, increase cooldown) (owner: Kevin).

9) Notes to self / random commands for digging deeper
- kubectl get events --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' -n infra | tail -n 200
- kubectl exec -it gpu-node-xyz-1 -- ls -l /dev | grep nvidia
- curl http://<node-exporter>:9100/metrics | grep gpu_ready
- prometheus query: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(node_boot_time_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- look at cloud-init logs on nodes: /var/log/cloud-init.log and /var/log/cloud-init-output.log

10) Open questions / unknowns
- Are we seeing driver installation failures only on certain instance types/regions? (need mapping)
- Is there any interaction with our node rotation/OS image patching that makes driver install slower?
- Should we move to baked images for all GPU instance types? cost/ops tradeoff.

End of scratchpad. Filing a concise runbook draft separately but keeping this as the noisy breadcrumbs for repro and debugging history.

-- Kevin
